takes.text: Storms are turning faster, and the days are six hours long.
Storms are steered by the spin, and that steering grows with the spin rate.
At a six hour day it is four times stronger than today.
At the edge of floating, seventeen times.
The calm of an ordinary afternoon would be gone, and nobody could forecast it, because nobody has seen a planet like this.
At a six hour day the Sun crosses from horizon to horizon in three hours.
The equator moves at about forty-one hundred and fifty miles an hour.
You are five and a half percent lighter.
Jumping takes you higher than it should, and every step feels slightly wrong.
If you're enjoying this, tap like and follow.
And the calendar is about to break.
